witness.quote: Every driver of a vehicle approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign
witness.reason: A governed approach at the fixed two-way intersection can realize stopping before an unmarked near-side crosswalk.
required_context: An eligible motor vehicle and driver with actual physical control.
Complete approach and crossing trace; distinguish unrelated pedestrian and delivery-device routes.
Establish eligible vehicle classification and driver attribution.
Establish intersection boundaries and opposing sidewalk connections defining the near-side crosswalk.
Establish sign orientation and governance of the subject approach.
Keep unrelated pedestrian and delivery-device routes distinct.
Near-side crosswalk boundaries established by opposing sidewalk lateral-line connections.
Observe approach, cessation, and subsequent crossing without adding a minimum stationary duration.
Stop-sign governance and qualifying two-way intersection geometry.
witness.subject_reason: This assignment uses the available motor_vehicle_driver, without extending the vehicle definition to excluded devices.

law.title: Designation of through highways and intersections requiring stop or yield (2)
law.text: Every driver of a vehicle approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway before entering the intersection.

activation_conditions: the subject is the driver of a vehicle
the subject is approaching an intersection whose approach is indicated by a stop sign

required_observations.note: a stop sign at the intersection
the sign faces the subject's approach
the subject's lane is an approach to the intersection the sign governs
the subject is approaching that intersection
the near-side crosswalk, marked or unmarked
a clearly marked stop line, if there is one
the intersection region and its boundary
where a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway first opens, when there is neither crosswalk nor stop line
'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic': the traffic on the intersecting highway in the subject's line of sight from the stopping point
the footprint crossing the crosswalk / stop line boundary

residue: which of the three halting references applies is a map question (is there a crosswalk, is there a marked stop line); the third is the first point from which approaching traffic is in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible), and only as good as the source's line-of-sight test
summary.subject: driver

timing_requirements.requirement: the halt occurs before the footprint crosses the halting reference — the near-side crosswalk, or the stop line if there is no crosswalk, or the point where the view of the intersecting highway opens if there is neither
a full stop, not a rolling minimum: speed at or below the drv.stopped epsilon for at least its span parameter
the halt precedes entering the intersection
